paper.title: Machine-Learning Prediction of Tumor Comorbidity and Cancer-Associated Mortality in Patients With Coronary Heart Disease: A 2-Stage Modeling Study.
paper.abstract:
Background: Coronary heart disease (CHD) with concomitant tumors is increasingly prevalent and is associated with a higher mortality. We aimed to develop 2 predictive models to enable early identification of tumor risk in patients with CHD and mortality risk in those with CHD and cancer.
Methods: We analyzed 134 141 patients with CHD treated at Tongji Hospital (Huazhong University of Science and Technology, Wuhan, Hubei, China) during 2001 to 2023. Data collected from the First Hospital of Peking University (Beijing, China) were used for external validation. We developed and evaluated 6 machine learning models (extreme gradient boosting, light gradient boosting machine, random forest, neural network, decision tree, and logistic regression). Model explainability was improved using Shapley additive explanation, and an online prediction platform was subsequently implemented.
Results: For the model of predicting tumor risk in patients with CHD, extreme gradient boosting showed the best performance in the test set (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve =0.935), achieving the lowest Brier score (0.080). Its sensitivity, accuracy, and F1 score were 0.740, 0.882, and 0.751, respectively. Meanwhile, light gradient boosting machine performed well for in-hospital mortality prediction in the test set (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve =0.965), achieving the lowest Brier score (0.019), and the highest sensitivity (0.677), and F1 score (0.599). The 2 models also showed good performance in the external validation, suggesting a degree of generalizability.
Conclusions: We constructed 2 predictive models to assess the risk of tumor and cancer-associated mortality in patients with CHD. The web platform assists clinicians in decision-making and patient management.

paper.title: RxReduce: a medication deprescribing agent framework leveraging large language models to optimize proton pump inhibitor use.
paper.abstract:
Objectives: Polypharmacy rates continue to rise which can lead to increased risk of adverse drug events. Deprescribing is essential but time-consuming, requiring extensive clinical note and chart review. We developed RxReduce, a large language model (LLM)-powered framework as a proof of concept that can assist with medication deprescribing.
Materials And Methods: RxReduce utilizes LLMs and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to evaluate patient data. Focusing on proton pump inhibitors, the system analyzes diagnoses and clinical notes to generate recommendations (Continue, Deprescribe, or Stop). To optimize accuracy, clinical notes were preprocessed into summaries before RAG retrieval.
Results: The optimized system achieved an F1 score of 0.84, significantly outperforming the baseline (0.70).
Conclusion: RxReduce demonstrates the viability of artificial intelligence-assisted deprescribing. By extracting key contextual insights, the framework reduces clinician burden and can be adapted for various medication classes to improve patient safety.

paper.title: Explainable age prediction using a transformer trained on diverse global electrocardiograms.
paper.abstract:
Aims: Artificial intelligence (AI) models trained on electrocardiograms (ECGs) can estimate age, with deviations from chronological age (Δage) serving as markers of accelerated cardiovascular ageing. We evaluated whether transformer-based AI models trained on globally diverse, heterogeneous ECG datasets outperform convolutional neural network (CNN)-based models in generalizability and physiological interpretability.
Methods And Results: Using 11 public datasets (435 203 recordings) from four continents and an independent external cohort (14 462 recordings), we trained and validated transformer and CNN architectures. The transformer model trained on global data achieved strong correlation with chronological age and maintained robust performance in the external cohort (r = 0.90), outperforming both a CNN trained on global data and a model trained exclusively on a homogenous population-based cohort (r = 0.88). Individuals with Δage ≥+8 years exhibited a two-fold increased mortality risk (hazard ratio = 2.08, 95% confidence interval 1.93-2.24). Explainability analysis identified the P-wave, particularly in lead V1, as the dominant contributor to age prediction, consistent with known electrophysiological changes associated with atrial remodelling and ageing. The model's attribution to early atrial conduction features was consistent across age strata, peaking in midlife (30-50 years), and correlated positively with disease burden, including hypertension and smoking.
Conclusion: Our findings establish that transformer models trained on globally heterogeneous data generalize well and can provide insights to plausible ageing signatures. Furthermore, Δage may offer insight into underlying physiological ageing processes and associated risk, though further validation is needed to define its clinical utility in risk stratification.

paper.title: Construction and validation of a 28-day mortality prediction model for refeeding syndrome in critically ill patients.
paper.abstract:
Background And Aims: Refeeding syndrome (RFS) is a common and serious metabolic reaction during nutritional support in critically ill patients, associated with substantially increased mortality risk and poor prognosis. Existing studies mainly focus on predicting its occurrence, while predictive models for 28-day mortality risk remain lacking. This study aimed to develop and validate an interpretable machine learning model to support short-term prognostic assessment in clinical practice.
Methods: Data for critically ill patients with RFS were extracted from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV, 2008-2019) as the internal cohort. A total of 8,705 patients were randomly assigned to training and test sets at a 7:3 ratio. Thirty-eight candidate variables were initially included, and feature selection was performed using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) logistic regression. Three machine learning models were subsequently constructed, and the optimal model was validated using two independent datasets. Model interpretability was enhanced using Shapley additive explanations (SHAP). Kaplan-Meier curves were used to compare survival between the high- and low-risk, and nomograms were constructed to facilitate clinical application.
Results: Nine variables were ultimately selected to construct the logistic regression model. The model demonstrated excellent discriminative performance and generalizability, with area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values of 0.821, 0.809, and 0.731 in the internal test set, external validation set I (MIMIC-III), and external validation set II (the Affiliated Hospital of Yangzhou University), respectively. SHAP analysis identified partial pressure of oxygen, mean blood glucose level, and age as the key prognostic factors and further revealed nonlinear effects among the variables. Kaplan-Meier survival curves confirmed that the model significantly distinguished between the high- and low-risk groups across all cohorts (all p < 0.05). Decision curve analysis showed that the model provided favorable clinical net benefit in both external validation cohorts.
Conclusion: The interpretable machine learning model developed in this study effectively predicts the 28-day mortality risk of RFS in critically ill patients, provides an objective reference for individualized clinical decision-making, and may help improve patient prognosis.

paper.title: Machine Learning-Based Prediction of Mortality in Patients With Mitral Regurgitation: Results From Two Nationwide, Prospective Studies.
paper.abstract: Mitral regurgitation (MR) is among the most prevalent valvular heart diseases. We developed and externally validated a machine learning (ML)-based mortality prediction model for patients with significant MR. From the ChinaValvular Heart Disease (China-VHD) registry, 6323 patients with moderate or greater MR were randomly split 7:3 into training and internal validation sets. Variables selected concordantly by Cox stepwise regression, Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO)-penalized Cox regression, and Boruta were retained. Seventeen ML and traditional models were compared. The final model was tested in the internal set and an external cohort of 4658 patients from the China Elderly Valve Disease (China-DVD) study. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis assessed interpretability. Fifteen predictors were identified. CatBoost performed best, with AUCs of 0.783 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.751-0.815) internally and 0.703 (0.678-0.728) externally, outperforming Cox (0.699), MitraScore (0.620), and EuroSCORE II (0.679). Age, NYHA class, and left ventricular ejection fraction were the top predictors. The model effectively distinguished high-risk from low-risk patients internally (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 5.49, p < 0.001) and externally (adjusted HR 3.05, p < 0.001). In conclusion, we developed and externally validated an ML-based mortality prediction model for MR irrespective of etiology or treatment strategy, with potential to improve risk stratification and clinical decision-making.

paper.title: CDKPredict: a clinicogenomic model for risk-adapted therapeutic intervention in breast cancer.
paper.abstract: Wide variation in outcomes is observed for patients with hormone-receptor-positive metastatic breast cancer (MBC) receiving first-line CDK4/6 inhibitors plus endocrine therapy (CDK4/6i+ET). Although front-line escalation strategies are beginning to enter clinical practice, assigning patients to intensified or de-intensified approaches remains challenging due to several mechanisms of resistance spanning tumor-intrinsic and host factors. To address this, we developed CDKPredict, an interpretable machine-learning model integrating baseline clinicopathologic and genomic features to predict outcomes from first-line CDK4/6i+ET. The model was trained on a densely annotated cohort of 1,264 patients and validated in a large multi-institutional external cohort (n=564, time-dependent AUC=0.74), stratifying patients into low-, intermediate-, and high-risk groups (median progression-free survival: 29.8, 14.7, and 8.0 months, respectively; hazard ratio [high vs low]=3.85, P=1.5x10-17). The model retained robust prognostication across clinically relevant subgroups and biomarker-selected populations and outperformed the current escalation criterion of treatment-free interval ≤12 months. Notably, CDKPredict demonstrated strong clinical and biological plausibility, with high-risk tumors featuring genomic and transcriptomic programs mechanistically linked to CDK4/6i+ET resistance, and higher-risk strata progressively enriched for actionable alterations. Finally, we developed CDKPredict-S, a pragmatic and scalable model requiring a restricted number of features intended for resource-variable settings, which was validated across two independent external cohorts totaling 1,019 patients and made publicly available. Collectively, CDKPredict provides a foundation for the prospective evaluation of risk-adapted, biomarker-informed therapeutic strategies.

paper.title: Explainable machine learning for 2-year functional outcomes in older adults with aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage in North China: external validation and health-system context.
paper.abstract:
Background: Older adults with aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH) have heterogeneous long-term outcomes, and differences in treatment pathways and hospital capacity may complicate early risk stratification.
Methods: This multicenter cohort study included adults aged ≥60 years with aSAH in North China. Of 1,132 admissions at four hospitals from January 2017 to September 2023, 914 patients with 2-year follow-up were divided 7:3 into training (n = 640) and internal-validation (n = 274) cohorts. An independent cohort screened 602 admissions from January 2017 to January 2021 and included 499 patients. Poor outcome was defined as modified Rankin Scale 3-6 at 2 years. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression with 10-fold cross-validation selected predictors, and 10 machine-learning algorithms were compared. Discrimination, calibration, decision-curve analysis, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) were evaluated.
Results: Among 1,413 patients, 583 (41.3%) had a poor 2-year outcome. Gradient boosting machine (GBM) AUCs were 0.863 (95% CI, 0.835-0.891), 0.834 (0.785-0.883), and 0.791 (0.749-0.833) in the training, internal-validation, and external-validation cohorts, respectively. External-validation accuracy was 0.752, sensitivity 0.661, specificity 0.808, precision 0.683, and F1 score 0.672. GBM had the highest external AUC point estimate but did not lead every classification metric. SHAP ranked Hunt-Hess grade, age, World Federation of Neurosurgical Societies grade, and treatment as the most influential features. Unadjusted survival differed across treatment and hospital-capacity strata (both log-rank p < 0.0001).
Conclusion: An explainable GBM retained moderate discrimination during external validation and may support admission-stage risk stratification in older adults with aSAH. The health-system findings are associative, and prospective recalibration, fairness assessment, and impact evaluation are required before clinical or public-health deployment.
